translationRepairs: Wang Song, vice minister of works and acting revenue overseer, was reassigned as vice minister of punishments in the Secretariat;
Wang Song, vice minister of works and acting revenue overseer, was reassigned as vice minister of punishments in the Department of State Affairs;
尚書刑部侍郎 is a Department of State Affairs (尚書省) post; Secretariat would be 中書. The replacement restores the correct institution without changing the rest of the sentence.
Vice Minister of Works and overseer of revenue Wang Song was changed to Vice Minister of Punishments in the Secretariat;
Vice Minister of Works and overseer of revenue Wang Song was changed to Vice Minister of Punishments in the Department of State Affairs;
In 尚書刑部侍郎, 尚書 names the Shangshu Department of State Affairs, not the Secretariat. The literal replacement is accurate.
Wu Chengfan, director in the ministry of granaries and drafting official, was made director in the armory and direct academician of the Secretariat-Chancellery Bureau.
Wu Chengfan, vice director of the Tuntian (military-farms) bureau and drafter of edicts, was made vice director of the armory bureau and direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

屯田員外郎 is vice director of the Tuntian (military-farms) bureau, not a granaries director; 庫部員外郎 is likewise a vice-directorship; 樞密院直學士 belongs to the Bureau of Military Affairs. The proposed offices match the Chinese.
The Director of the Ministry of Granaries and Drafting Official Wu Chengfan was appointed Director of the Armory and direct academician of the Secretariat-Chancellery Bureau.
The Vice Director of the Tuntian Bureau and Drafter of Edicts Wu Chengfan was appointed Vice Director of the Armory and direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
The literal line misrenders 屯田 as granaries, 員外郎 as director, and 樞密院 as the Secretariat-Chancellery. The replacement corrects office, rank, and institution.
On bingshen an order named Ma Xiege, military commissioner of the Wuqing army, military commissioner of the Weiwu army instead.
On bingshen an order named Ma Xi'e, military commissioner of the Wuqing army, as military commissioner of the Weiwu army instead.

希萼 is Xi'e, so Ma Xiege is a real romanization error, but the proposed sentence remains ungrammatical ('named X, title, title instead'). The revision keeps the original wording and inserts the missing 'as' after the correct name.
For temple taboo level-tone characters, the other three tones of yu are not tabooed;
For temple taboo level-tone characters, the other three tones are not tabooed;
余三聲 is 'the remaining three tones,' not tones of the syllable yu. The literal had misread 余 as a phonetic.
On dinghai in the fourth month, Lu Zhan, vice minister of personnel, was made left vice director of the Secretariat.
On dinghai in the fourth month, Lu Zhan, vice minister of personnel, was made left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
尚書左丞 is Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, not of the Secretariat (中書).
In the fourth month, on dinghai, Vice Minister of Personnel Lu Zhan was appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
In the fourth month, on dinghai, Vice Minister of Personnel Lu Zhan was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
The same 尚書左丞 belongs to the Shangshu Department of State Affairs. The literal replacement is accurate.
On wuchen the late military commissioner of Zhenwu, Li Siben, was posthumously granted grand guardian.
On wuchen the late military commissioner of Zhenwu, Li Siben, was posthumously granted grand commandant.
贈太尉 is a posthumous Grand Commandant. Grand guardian would be 太保, which the previous sentence uses for a different man.
On wuchen, the late Military Commissioner of Zhenwu Li Siben was posthumously granted Grand Guardian.
On wuchen, the late Military Commissioner of Zhenwu Li Siben was posthumously granted Grand Commandant.
Chinese 太尉 does not mean Grand Guardian; the literal replacement restores Grand Commandant.
On jiashen Wang Jumin, grand mentor of the heir apparent, was put in charge of the monopoly salt administration at the Anyi and Jie pools.
On jiashen Wang Jumin, chief of the household of the heir apparent, was put in charge of the monopoly salt administration at the Anyi and Jie pools.
太子詹事 is chief of the heir apparent's household, not Grand Mentor (太傅). The replacement matches the office.
On jiashen, Wang Jumin, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was appointed to oversee the monopoly salt administration of the Anyi and Jie county pools.
On jiashen, Wang Jumin, Chief of the Household of the Heir Apparent, was appointed to oversee the monopoly salt administration of the Anyi and Jie county pools.
The literal likewise mistranslates 太子詹事 as Grand Mentor; Chief of the Household of the Heir Apparent is correct.

On bingwu, the first day of the seventh month, Xue Rong, Left Remonstrance Counselor; Lü Qi, Director of the Palace Library; Liu Hao, Transport Office Vice Director and concurrent Supervising Censor; Situ Xu, Director in the Ministry of Punishments; and Zhang Rentuan, Senior Rectifier of the Court of Judicial Review, were jointly assigned to review and revise the compiled edicts of the Tang reign of Emperor Mingzong.

On bingwu, the first day of the seventh month, Xue Rong, Left Remonstrance Counselor; Lü Qi, Director of the Palace Library; Liu Hao, Transport Office Vice Director and concurrent Supervising Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs; Situ Xu, Director in the Ministry of Punishments; and Zhang Rentuan, Senior Rectifier of the Court of Judicial Review, were jointly assigned to review and revise the compiled edicts of the Tang reign of Emperor Mingzong.
The idiomatic line omits 知雜事 on Liu Hao's concurrent 侍御史 charge. Restoring 'in charge of miscellaneous affairs' matches the Chinese.
On renwu, the Weifu army front reported that the former Prefect of Chan Zhou Feng Hui had come over from the rebel city.
On renwu, the Weifu army front reported that the former Prefect of Chan, Feng Hui, had come over from the rebel city.
前澶州刺史馮暉 names Feng Hui, former prefect of Chan; 'Zhou' is an invented surname parsed out of 澶州.
On jichou, the former Prefect of Chan Zhou Feng Hui was appointed Honorary Grand Guardian and Military Commissioner of the Yicheng Army.
On jichou, the former Prefect of Chan, Feng Hui, was appointed Honorary Grand Guardian and Military Commissioner of the Yicheng Army.
The Chinese again has only 馮暉 after 澶州刺史; the invented Zhou must be removed.
On wuxu Yan prefecture reported that the Yellow River had broken through its banks on the Yanggu county border.
On wuxu Yun prefecture reported that the Yellow River had broken through its banks on the Yanggu county border.
鄆州 is Yun prefecture; Yan would render 燕 or 兗. Yanggu is reported from Yun.
On wuxu, Yan Prefecture reported the Yellow River had burst its banks at the border of Yanggu County.
On wuxu, Yun Prefecture reported the Yellow River had burst its banks at the border of Yanggu County.
The literal's Yan Prefecture is the same misreading of 鄆州; Yun Prefecture is correct.

On maoyin an edict raised Feng Dao, minister of works and grand councilor, to first rank with sixteen gate halberds; Sang Weihan and Li Song, vice directors and grand councilors, received twelve each.
On yimao an edict raised Feng Dao, minister of works and grand councilor, to first rank with sixteen gate halberds; Sang Weihan and Li Song, vice directors and grand councilors, received twelve each.
乙卯 is the sexagenary day yimao. maoyin would be 卯寅; the surrounding days 壬子 then 乙卯 confirm yimao.

On maoyin, an edict granted Minister of Works and concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor Feng Dao first rank, with sixteen gate halberds; Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Grand Councilors Sang Weihan and Li Song were granted twelve gate halberds each.

On yimao, an edict granted Minister of Works and concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor Feng Dao first rank, with sixteen gate halberds; Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Grand Councilors Sang Weihan and Li Song were granted twelve gate halberds each.
The literal shares the same false reading of 乙卯 as maoyin; yimao is the correct day name.
On chouzi the king of Khotan, Yang Renmei, sent envoys with tribute goods.
On yichou the king of Khotan, Yang Renmei, sent envoys with tribute goods.
乙丑 is yichou, not chouzi. The next dated day 丙寅 follows yichou in the cycle.
On chouzi, King Yang Renmei of Khotan sent envoys presenting local products.
On yichou, King Yang Renmei of Khotan sent envoys presenting local products.
The literal's chouzi is the same inversion of 乙丑; yichou is correct.
Li Shi, Yanguang's former staff officer, was made honorary right vice director and Bozhou training commissioner;
Li Shi, deputy military commissioner of the Tianxiong Army and honorary Minister of Punishments, was made honorary right vice director and Bozhou training commissioner;
The Chinese titles Li Shi 天雄軍節度副使、檢校刑部尚書; 'Yanguang's former staff officer' is invented and omits both offices.
On yihai in the tenth month Wang Jigong of Fujian sent envoys with tribute goods.
On yihai in the tenth month Wang Jigong, Military Commissioner of Fujian, sent envoys with tribute goods.
福建節度使王繼恭 names Wang Jigong as military commissioner of Fujian; dropping that office is a real omission.
Fan Yanguang of Yan reported his arrival in his jurisdiction.
Fan Yanguang of Yun reported his arrival in his jurisdiction.
鄆州範延光 is Fan Yanguang of Yun, not Yan.
Fan Yanguang of Yan Prefecture memorialized his arrival in his jurisdiction.
Fan Yanguang of Yun Prefecture memorialized his arrival in his jurisdiction.
The literal's Yan Prefecture misreads 鄆州; Yun Prefecture matches the Chinese.

On renchen Sang Weihan, controller of the secretariat-chancellery bureau, vice director, grand councilor, and grand academician, was also made minister of war; the secretariat-chancellery controllers were abolished.

On renchen Sang Weihan, Privy Councilor, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, and Grand Academician of the Hall for Advancing Worthies, was also made Minister of War; all were removed as Privy Councilors.
樞密使 is privy councilor, not a Secretariat-Chancellery controller; 中書侍郎平章事 and 集賢殿大學士 are separate titles, and 皆罷樞密使 records dismissal as privy councilors.

On renchen, Sang Weihan—Controller of the Secretariat-Chancellery Bureau, Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, and Grand Academician of the Hall for Advancing Worthies—was additionally appointed Minister of War; all were removed as controllers of the Secretariat-Chancellery Bureau.

On renchen, Sang Weihan—Privy Councilor, Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, and Grand Academician of the Hall for Advancing Worthies—was additionally appointed Minister of War; all were removed as Privy Councilors.
Both 樞密使 clauses are mistranslated as Secretariat-Chancellery controllers; Privy Councilor is correct in both.
According to the Comprehensive Mirror's examination of differences citing Gaozu's veritable record, Weihan and Li Song were both removed as controllers.)〉
According to the Comprehensive Mirror's examination of differences citing Gaozu's veritable record, Weihan and Li Song were both removed as privy councilors.)〉
The commentary's 並罷樞密使 means both men were removed as privy councilors, not generic controllers.

According to the Examination of Differences in the Comprehensive Mirror citing the Veritable Record of Emperor Gaozu of Jin, Weihan and Li Song were both removed as controllers of the Secretariat-Chancellery Bureau.)〉
According to the Examination of Differences in the Comprehensive Mirror citing the Veritable Record of Emperor Gaozu of Jin, Weihan and Li Song were both removed as Privy Councilors.)〉
The literal again renders 樞密使 as Secretariat-Chancellery controllers; Privy Councilors matches 並罷樞密使.
On jiachen in the eleventh month Wu Juan was promoted to director of metals and drafting official, and Wu Chengfan to director of sacrifices and drafting official.

On jiachen in the eleventh month Wu Juan, Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Vice Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices, was promoted to Director of the Bureau of Metals and drafting official, and Wu Chengfan, Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Vice Director of the Armory Bureau, to Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices and drafting official.
The Chinese names each man's prior 樞密直學士 post and 祠部/庫部員外郎 rank before the 郎中 promotions; omitting those offices is a real loss.

In the eleventh month, on jiachen, Wu Juan, direct academician of the Secretariat-Chancellery Bureau and Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices, was promoted to Director of the Bureau of Metals and Drafting Official; Wu Chengfan, direct academician and Director of the Armory, was promoted to Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices and Drafting Official.

In the eleventh month, on jiachen, Wu Juan, Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Vice Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices, was promoted to Director of the Bureau of Metals and Drafting Official; Wu Chengfan, Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Vice Director of the Armory Bureau, was promoted to Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices and Drafting Official.
樞密直學士 belongs to the Bureau of Military Affairs, and 員外郎 is vice director, not director. The replacement corrects institution and rank.
On yisi Fan Yanguang of Yan came to court.
On yisi Fan Yanguang of Yun came to court.
鄆州 is Yun; Yan would be 燕 or 兗.
On yisi, Fan Yanguang of Yan Prefecture came to court.
On yisi, Fan Yanguang of Yun Prefecture came to court.
The literal's Yan Prefecture is the same misreading of 鄆州.

Qian Yuankuan, Military Commissioner of the Zhongwu and Jianwu armies, Honorary Grand Preceptor, concurrent Chief Councilor, and Prefect of Suzhou and Chen, was appointed Grand Mentor; Qian Yuanshan, Military Commissioner of the Qinghai Army and Prefect of Guang, was appointed Honorary Grand Commandant and concurrent Chief Councilor, and his name was changed to Yuanyi.

Qian Yuankuan, Military Commissioner of the Zhongwu and Jianwu armies, Honorary Grand Preceptor, concurrent Chief Councilor, and Prefect of Suzhou and Cheng, was appointed Grand Mentor; Qian Yuanshan, Military Commissioner of the Qinghai Army and Prefect of Guang, was appointed Honorary Grand Commandant and concurrent Chief Councilor, and his name was changed to Yuanyi.
誠州 is Cheng, not Chen (陳). The rest of the literal sentence is otherwise aligned with the Chinese.
Yang Guangyuan of Weibo was made grand guardian, Luoyang regent, concurrent Heyang military commissioner, and overseer of the six armies and palace guards.
Yang Guangyuan of Weibo was made acting grand commandant, Luoyang regent, concurrent Heyang military commissioner, and overseer of the six armies and palace guards.
守太尉 is acting Grand Commandant; grand guardian would be 太保.
Yang Guangyuan, Military Commissioner of Weibo, was appointed Grand Guardian, Regent of Luoyang, concurrent Military Commissioner of Heyang, and overseer of the six armies and palace guards.
Yang Guangyuan, Military Commissioner of Weibo, was appointed acting Grand Commandant, Regent of Luoyang, concurrent Military Commissioner of Heyang, and overseer of the six armies and palace guards.
The literal's Grand Guardian misreads 守太尉; acting Grand Commandant is correct.
On gengxu Fan Yanguang of Yan begged to retire; the edict refused.
On gengxu Fan Yanguang of Yun begged to retire; the edict refused.
鄆州範延光 is Fan Yanguang of Yun, not Yan.
On gengxu, Fan Yanguang of Yan Prefecture submitted a memorial begging to retire; the edict did not grant it.
On gengxu, Fan Yanguang of Yun Prefecture submitted a memorial begging to retire; the edict did not grant it.
The literal repeats the Yan misreading of 鄆州.

Chonggui, senior general of the heir apparent's Right Golden guard, was made honorary grand mentor and Kaifeng metropolitan magistrate, enfeoffed as prince of Zheng, with three thousand additional households' fief income.

Chonggui, the heir apparent and senior general of the Right Golden Guard, was made honorary grand mentor and Kaifeng metropolitan magistrate, enfeoffed as prince of Zheng, with three thousand additional households' fief income.
皇太子右金吾衛上將軍重貴 titles Chonggui himself as heir apparent and senior general of the Right Golden Guard, not as an officer of a separate heir-apparent guard.

Chonggui, Senior General of the Right Golden Guard of the Heir Apparent, was appointed Honorary Grand Mentor and Kaifeng metropolitan magistrate, enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng, with fief income increased by three thousand households.

Chonggui, the Heir Apparent and Senior General of the Right Golden Guard, was appointed Honorary Grand Mentor and Kaifeng metropolitan magistrate, enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng, with fief income increased by three thousand households.
The literal attaches 皇太子 to the guard rather than to 重貴; the replacement restores the standard title string.

Ma Jirong, presenting envoy of the Great Treasure State of Khotan and honorary Grand Commandant, was made Grand General Who Guards the State; deputy envoy Zhang Zaitong, Yellow Gate General and Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, was made acting Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud; and supervising envoy Wu Shungui, Palace Head Director of Audience and Drafting Master of Ceremonies, was made acting Vice Director of Palace Buildings.

On wuyin, Ma Jirong, presenting envoy of the Great Treasure State of Khotan and honorary Grand Commandant, was made Grand General Who Guards the State; deputy envoy Zhang Zaitong, Yellow Gate General and Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, was made acting Chamberlain of the Court of the Imperial Insignia; and supervising envoy Wu Shungui, Palace Head Director of Audience and Drafting Master of Ceremonies, was made acting Vice Director of Palace Buildings.
The line opens 戊寅 and appoints Zhang Zaitong 試衛尉卿, the Court of the Imperial Insignia, not the Imperial Stud (太僕). The replacement restores the date and office.

An order appointed Ma Jirong, presenting envoy of the Great Treasure State of Khotan and honorary Grand Commandant, as Grand General Who Guards the State; Zhang Zaitong, Deputy Envoy, Yellow Gate General, and Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, as Acting Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud; and Wu Shungui, supervising envoy, Palace Head Director of Audience, and Drafting Master of Ceremonies, as Acting Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

An order on wuyin appointed Ma Jirong, presenting envoy of the Great Treasure State of Khotan and honorary Grand Commandant, as Grand General Who Guards the State; Zhang Zaitong, Deputy Envoy, Yellow Gate General, and Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, as Acting Chamberlain of the Court of the Imperial Insignia; and Wu Shungui, supervising envoy, Palace Head Director of Audience, and Drafting Master of Ceremonies, as Acting Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
The literal likewise drops 戊寅 and renders 衛尉卿 as Imperial Stud; Chamberlain of the Court of the Imperial Insignia is the correct office.
Li Congchang, Dragon Martial commander, died; court audiences were suspended for one day, and he was posthumously granted grand guardian.
Li Congchang, Dragon Martial commander, died; court audiences were suspended for one day, and he was posthumously granted grand commandant.
贈太尉 is Grand Commandant; grand guardian would be 太保.
Li Congchang, Commander of the Dragon Martial Army, died; court audiences were suspended for one day; he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian.
Li Congchang, Commander of the Dragon Martial Army, died; court audiences were suspended for one day; he was posthumously granted Grand Commandant.
The literal's Grand Guardian is the same mistranslation of 太尉.
